description: Phase B step 1: twin-only feasibility screen of the quad-pendulum controllers on the realistic rigs of realism.json (design/screen.py; raw runs in design/_screen/, not in git). Truth: the Lagrangian twin with the realism effects, RK4 with 8 substeps per 1 ms sample. Firmware replica: 1 kHz, the design's tables and LQR, sensors, delay and current loop, rates from filtered differences ('diff', the baseline) or an EKF on the nominal realistic model ('ekf'). Pass ('ok'): the run finishes, the swing-up is caught, every link within 2 deg of upright over the last 2 s, base travel within the controller's limit. Scenarios: swing-up from the hanging rest; balance from a 2 deg lean per link with a 50 ms tip push (the design's push).

effects.mass: encoder boards, magnets and cables lumped into the links; link and base mass, length and COM spread
effects.fbase: base Coulomb + viscous friction (cart: linear guide, belt, motor; rotary: arm bearing, motor)
effects.cable: cable springs and dampers across the joints and along the base
effects.sensor: 14-bit joint encoders with white noise (0.03 deg rms nominal), base encoder
effects.loop: 2 ms whole-sample delay + 0.3 ms current loop

verdict.cart: Feasible, with conditions. The existing full-travel controller (unchanged) passes all effects together at the nominal values ONLY with (1) the EKF (filtered differences fail with the AS5048-class encoders at every tau_f from 2 to 20 ms), (2) base Coulomb compensation (fc = nominal tc_base), and (3) pendulum-joint Coulomb friction of at most about 5e-5 N m per joint. At the assumed 2e-4 N m of small ball bearings the balance limit-cycles at 5-10 deg and no controller tried avoids it (gain scaling, robust minimax K search, lower-gain redesign). Even inside the budget the margin is thin: Monte Carlo over the realism ranges (tc_joint fixed at 5e-5) passes 11/24 swing-ups and 9/24 balances with the EKF (most failures are 2-3.7 deg limit cycles, a few diverge), 0/24 with filtered differences. Better joint encoders change this: with 16-bit, 0.005 deg encoders all effects pass with both estimators; with 18-bit, 0.001 deg (optical/inductive class) they pass with a third of the force noise.
verdict.cart_short: Same as the full-travel cart (it shares the balance LQR): all effects pass with EKF + compensation at tc_joint 5e-5 (swing-up 0.75 deg, balance 1.12 deg, peak travel 0.42 m of 0.5 m), fail at 2e-4; Monte Carlo 13/24 swing-ups, 9/24 balances.
verdict.rotary_quad: Not feasible as a built rig. The balance alone limit-cycles at 2-5 deg with only 2e-5 N m of joint Coulomb friction (10x below small ball bearings) and diverges from 5e-5 N m on (light 30 g, 0.15 m links: the bearing friction is about 1 % of a link's gravity torque). The swing-up (7 s, torque margin, redesigned on the realistic mass) is robust to the base friction, cables, 2 ms delay and ripple, but needs practically perfect rates: filtered differences with tau_f >= 2 ms fail even on exact positions, and the EKF fails with 0.001 deg rms encoder noise. Heavier links (80-100 g, 0.2-0.25 m) still limit-cycle at 4-9 deg at 2e-4 N m.
verdict.rotary_triple_proposal: A triple rotary with heavier, longer links is the stepping stone: links 0.2/0.2/0.25 m, 80/80/100 g on a 0.25 m arm keep the balance limit cycle at 0.6-0.8 deg at 1e-4 N m and 1.6-2.0 deg at 2e-4 N m (exact sensors, LQR, no delay); the quad with the same links gives 2.0-3.7 deg and 4.3-8.6 deg. The triple's swing-up is not screened yet (next step: design it on the realistic model, then the same ablation and Monte Carlo).
verdict.order: Cart first: the existing controllers pass the realistic model with an EKF, base friction compensation and selected low-friction bearings, and the cart has authority margin in the swing-up (peak force 65-78 % of the 40 N limit; the balance-with-push run with encoder noise touches the limit briefly). The rotary needs a new rig (triple, heavier links) and a new design.

recommendations: Joint bearings: budget 5e-5 N m Coulomb per pendulum joint for the cart quad (measure the bearings: run-out test of the free swing decay; open or lightly oiled, unshielded miniature bearings, low preload); 2e-4 N m (typical shielded small ball bearings) is not good enough.

Firmware: an EKF (or a comparable model-based observer) on the realistic nominal model; keep filtered differences only as the baseline. Cart tuning: process noise q_acc = (1, 10) (base, links); (0.3, 3) is too slow, (3, 30) and up diverge.
Base: Coulomb compensation fc_base tanh(v/2 eps) with fc_base = the measured carriage + belt friction.
Encoders: AS5048-class (14 bit, 0.03 deg) works only with the EKF and with little margin; 16-bit encoders with 0.005 deg noise make the cart robust with either estimator.

Lower balance gains do not help the cart: the lower-gain redesign (cart_real, LQR weights / 100) fails the balance with the extra link mass alone (5.8 deg) and every effect after it; the existing gains stay.

ablation_cart_current_controller.setup: nominal realism, base compensation 1.0, EKF q_acc (1, 10); tail deviation deg swing-up / balance; ok in brackets

tc_joint_5e-5.all_ekf: 0.76 / 1.12 (ok), u rms 7.0 N, balance peak u at the limit briefly

ablation_cart_current_controller.note: with compensation on but no base friction the compensation itself chatters (1.5 deg); without compensation the base friction alone gives 1.5 deg

encoder_grade_cart.setup: current controller, tc_joint 5e-5, all effects, compensation 1.0; swing-up / balance tail deg, u rms N

monte_carlo_cart.setup: 24 uniform draws over the realism ranges, tc_joint fixed at 5e-5, all effects, compensation 1.0, EKF (1, 10)
monte_carlo_cart.drivers: no single parameter dominates (|corr| < 0.6 with the log tail deviation): cable damping, base viscous friction, joint viscous friction, ripple and a fast current loop all add

limit_cycle_joint_coulomb.setup: balance from a 1 deg lean, realistic design rig, only joint Coulomb on, exact sensors, no delay; max link deviation over the last 3 s of 8 s, for LQR weight scales 0.001-10

linear_robustness.setup: discrete closed loop with the 2-sample delay, spectral radius (> 1 unstable) vs viscous joint damping b (a sticking Coulomb joint sweeps b from 0 to infinity)
linear_robustness.robust_K_search: minimax over b (Nelder-Mead/Powell from the LQR and its variants): best worst case cart 1.019 (b <= 0.05) and 1.021 (b <= 10), rotary 1.027; no K found that is stable for every joint damping (local search: not found, not proven impossible)

rotary.current_controller: swing-up fails with the encoder/cable/link mass (+22 %) alone, with 2 ms delay alone and with the sensors alone; balance fails with the sensors and with joint Coulomb 5e-5 (6-7 deg)
rotary.redesign_rotary_real: designed on the realistic nominal mass: T_s 7 s, |u| <= 0.7 u_max in the plan, 4 swings, r 30 / r_tv 10. With the realistic mass on: base friction, cables, 2 ms delay, ripple each pass (swing-up tail 0.003-0.35 deg); sensors fail (14-bit and 18-bit, with and without noise, except 18-bit noise-free with the EKF: 0.59 deg); joint Coulomb 5e-5 gives 8.8-9.5 deg
rotary.balance_redesign: passes every effect except the sensors at 14 bit; with 16-bit 0.005 deg encoders the balance passes all effects (1.0-1.7 deg) at tc_joint 0

commands: uv run examples/quad-pendulum/design/screen.py redesign cart_real | rotary_real
uv run examples/quad-pendulum/design/screen.py mc cart,cart_short --n 24 --est ekf,diff --comp 1.0 --ekf-q "[1,10]" --p '{"tc_joint": 5e-5}'
